text:
A: Hiya! I'm Stacey. Ooh, you look like a teacher, I said that about your photo.
B: Ha, everyone says that! It's the lanyard. Gemma, I'm Head of Maths at a school in Nottingham. I'm in Beeston.
A: I'm Sutton-in-Ashfield! We're practically neighbours, duck.
B: Oh, brilliant, someone local. What do you do, Stacey?
A: Care assistant at a care home. Older people, a lot of dementia. Three long days a week.
B: Oh, that's hard work. My mum was a dinner lady and then a TA, and she always said the caring jobs are the ones nobody pays properly.
A: She's not wrong. But I love it, honestly. The families always ask for me. One daughter brought me flowers last week just for doing her mum's hair nice.
B: Aw, that's lovely. That's the bit that matters, isn't it? It's the same with the kids, they remember if you remembered them.
A: Exactly that. I'm doing my Level 3 at the minute through work. Well, I'm meant to be. I'm a bit behind on the written bits, if I'm honest.
B: Oh, everyone's behind on the written bits. I'm behind on my marking, look, there's a stack of books right behind me.
A: Ha! See, I feel better now. I've got Kai doing his GCSEs this year and his maths is a disaster. He just sits on his Xbox.
B: What tier's he doing? Foundation or higher?
A: Erm, I don't actually know, lol. Foundation, I think? Is that the easy one?
B: It's the one where he can still get a good pass, so don't let anyone tell you it's easy. Honestly, half of it's confidence. Kids think they can't do maths because somebody once told them so. If he gets the basics, percentages, ratio, he'll be fine.
A: Will you come round mine and tell him that?
B: Ha, I'd have to charge you! No, I mean it though. Get him doing ten minutes on an evening. Does your fella help?
A: Dean? He drives a forklift. He says he's never needed algebra once in his life.
B: They all say that! My Rob's an electrician and he says the same, and then he's measuring cable runs all day.
A: Ha, I'll tell Dean that. Do you watch Love Island?
B: Not really, I'm more Strictly and Bake Off with my daughter. And Gogglebox. I cry at everything though, I'm terrible.
A: Aw, me too. I cried at the darts once.
B: The darts?
A: Someone's mum was in the crowd! Don't judge me! Do you go away much?
B: Same place in Majorca three years running. And half-term it's a caravan at Skegness with my mum.
A: No way! We go to Skeg, my mum's side have got caravans. We might have been there the same week and not known it.
B: Oh, wouldn't that be funny. I bet you were the ones having the party next door.
A: Probably, to be fair. We're loud. Ooh, are you Forest or Mansfield?
B: Forest, God help me. Rob and Josh have got season tickets, so if they lose I just keep my head down all weekend, do you know what I mean?
A: Ha, Dean takes me to Mansfield. I only go for the bar, if I'm honest. Do you...
